### Observed differences

- In the later window, A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 each occur in all 200 traces (about one occurrence per trace, at a mean position of roughly 0.39 of the trace); before, A30–A32 were not observed at all and A20/A21 appeared in about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, POS003, POS004, POS009, POS010, POS011]
- These five activities now run together without a fixed order among themselves: every pair co-occurs in all 200 later traces with both orders in similar shares (for example, A20 before A21 in about 52 in 100 traces and A21 before A20 in about 47 in 100). [REL024, REL029, REL030, REL031, REL040, REL041, REL042, REL073, REL074, REL079]
- In the later window, each of the five precedes A33 in about 97–99 in 100 of their joint traces, whereas before, A33 typically ran without them (for example, A33 without A20 in about 99–100 in 100 traces); A33's mean position moved later, from about 0.39 to about 0.48 of the trace. [REL032, REL043, REL075, REL080, REL084, POS012]
- A04 now appears in about 72 in 100 traces, up from about 10 in 100 (mean occurrences 0.11 → 0.79), and sits earlier in the trace (mean position about 0.54 → 0.33); its outgoing transitions shifted from a spread over A52 (about 23 in 100), A16 (about 18 in 100) and many small shares to mostly the five activities (A20 about 22, A32 about 20, A31/A21/A30 about 15 each per 100 outgoing transitions), and A04 precedes each of them in about 64–65 in 100 traces (in about 27 in 100 later traces the block runs without A04). [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, REL002, REL003, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- A48 now leads to A04 in about 70 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (before: mainly A19, A22, A23, A24 and A25 at about 13–25 in 100 each, A04 only about 1–2 in 100), and A48 immediately precedes A04 in about 99 in 100 later cases (against 3 of 4 earlier cases, a weak base); A48's mean position moved earlier, about 0.33 → 0.28. [DIR013, LAG001, POS013, REL012]
- A19, A23, A24 and A25, previously present in about 14–27 in 100 traces, are not observed in the later window, and A22 dropped from about 25 in 100 to about 1 in 100; before, each of them led almost exclusively to A33 (about 91–96 in 100 of their outgoing transitions). [OCC004, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, DIR003, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009]
- Smaller shifts: A08 and A10 now appear in about 7–8 in 100 traces, down from about 18 in 100, while A51 and A53 routing is essentially unchanged (A53 immediately before A54 in about 87 → 97 in 100). [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR014, DIR015, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that a block of five previously unobserved activities — A20, A21, A30, A31 and A32 — now executes in every case, in no fixed order among themselves, between A48/A04 and A33: A04 participates in most cases (about 72 in 100, up from about 10 in 100) and directly follows A48, while the activities that previously ran directly before A33 in a minority of cases (A19, A22, A23, A24, A25) are no longer observed. [OCC001, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, DIR001, DIR013, LAG001, REL002, REL003, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL024, REL032, REL043, REL073, REL075, REL079, REL080, REL084]

The signs are direct and consistent across occurrence, routing, relational, positional and lag evidence: participation moves from 0 or about 1 in 200 to 200 of 200 traces for the five activities and to 0 for the old ones; the routing profiles of A04 and A48 point at the chain A48 → A04 → block → A33; and A33's later mean position matches the block now running before it. The screening comparison also shows the set of qualified items far exceeds what an unchanged process produces (130 control-flow items against roughly 1 expected without change). [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, DIR001, DIR013, LAG001, REL011, REL012, POS012, POS013]

Limitations: most relational items restate one underlying trace change, so they are not independent confirmations; zero participation only means an activity was not observed, so the evidence cannot rule out that A19, A22, A23, A24 and A25 still exist in the process but were simply not chosen in the later sample; and the evidence supports no statement about why the behaviour differs. [OCC004, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]

Other differences: A08 and A10 became rarer (about 18 in 100 traces before, about 7–8 in 100 after), while A51 and A53 routing stayed essentially the same. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR014, DIR015, LAG002]
